newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower, meal down on imports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower, meal down on imports.

text.p: CBOT soymeal and soyoil futures ended lower, with soymeal down sharply on worries over an influx of soymeal imports from South America, analysts said.
"Meal was lower on imports and on the story about Tyson saying they would take soymeal from South America," said Anne Frick, oilseed analyst with Prudential Securities.
On Tuesday, a spokesman for U.S. poultry giant Tyson Foods, Inc. said the company would accept soymeal from suppliers that contained soybeans from South America.
Typically, U.S. companies shun the use of farm products from other countries.
However, record-low supplies of U.S. soybeans and high prices have caused U.S. exporters and crushers to use less expensive Brazilian soybeans in some cases, traders and analysts said.

After climbing as much as 0.50 cent per lb on Monday, soyoil futures posted a sharp retreat on Tuesday in response to heavy soybean losses and ideas that the market was overbought, CBOT floor traders said.
CBOT soymeal futures ended $1.50 to $4.10 per ton lower, with July down $4.10 at $283.10 a ton. Soyoil ended 0.07 to 0.29 cent per lb lower, with July down 0.29 at 23.85 cents.
